entries.feature: Codex in the ChatGPT desktop app
entries.audit_feature: Auditor desktop workbench
entries.codex_behavior: The desktop experience brings projects, chats, agent activity, files, execution tools, review, configuration and execution-location choices into one workspace. Available features differ by operating system, account and client release.
entries.trigger: The auditor opens a workspace or starts a task.
entries.audit_action: Coordinate audit work through conversation while keeping source material, workpapers, calculations and agent progress inspectable beside it.
outputs: Links to existing files and tools
entries.auditor_control: Choose the task and execution location, inspect changes, steer work, and open the same saved artifacts in external editors.
entries.example: Ask for a loan-interest reconciliation, inspect its workbook beside the chat, then continue reviewing that workbook in Excel.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Retain the working experience while replacing developer emphasis with audit materials. Embedded editing depth and platform parity require validation; a desktop workspace alone does not establish formal audit records.

entries.audit_feature: Audit workspaces and focused work conversations
entries.codex_behavior: Projects group files, instructions and chats; local projects can attach folders. Each chat retains its own transcript. Navigation supports search, renaming, pinning and archival. CLI and IDE project context follow their directory or workspace.
entries.trigger: Start a new assignment, standalone investigation or conversation within an existing workspace.
entries.audit_action: Group related audit work and start separate conversations for distinct outcomes, with explicit access to the relevant files and guidance.
entries.auditor_control: Select attached folders, rename or pin recurring work, and archive or restore completed conversations.
entries.example: Keep rate-change testing, borrower communications review and report drafting in separate chats under the same assignment.
entries.adaptation_boundary: A workspace can support ad hoc work or a formal engagement. Folder organisation and pinning do not themselves grant access or enforce confidentiality; primary-folder instruction discovery needs explicit treatment.

audit_enhancements.change: Use assignment, client and reporting-period labels while retaining standalone tasks.
audit_enhancements.why: Auditors must distinguish related work without forcing every request into an engagement.

audit_enhancements.change: Show which instructions and folders belong to the current task.
audit_enhancements.why: Similar files from different periods or clients can otherwise be mistaken for the applicable material.

entries.audit_feature: Auditor command-line and batch work client
entries.codex_behavior: The CLI supports interactive investigation, planning, file edits, tool execution and review within a directory. Non-interactive codex exec can run scripted tasks and emit structured events for other processes to consume.
entries.trigger: An auditor or analyst starts an interactive command, or an authorised job invokes a saved task.
entries.audit_action: Offer the same audit assistance through a terminal for technical auditors, data analysts and repeatable batch jobs.
entries.auditor_control: Set working directory, execution scope and requested output; interrupt interactive work or review batch results before relying on them.
entries.example: An IT auditor runs a saved access-review procedure against an approved directory export and receives an exceptions file.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Keep the CLI as a legitimate surface rather than forcing all auditors into it. Installed analysis tools, input formats and event consumers determine what an individual job can do.

subfeatures.audit: Interactive investigation of an audit folder
Reusable headless audit jobs
Machine-readable job progress and results
Continue eligible work through another execution surface

audit_enhancements.change: Accept named audit procedures and structured procedure parameters through the command surface.
audit_enhancements.why: Repeated analyses need explicit period, population and criteria inputs rather than only a freeform prompt.

entries.audit_feature: Audit task command and session controls
entries.codex_behavior: CLI and slash commands manage sessions, plans, goals, models, permissions, tools and review. Commands also expose context compaction, configuration, keymaps and reconnect controls. Maturity varies: some cloud and remote-control commands remain experimental.
entries.trigger: The auditor invokes a task control through a command, shortcut or equivalent interface action.
entries.audit_action: Expose the same task-management operations using audit-friendly labels while preserving access for power users.
entries.auditor_control: Explicitly choose operations that change execution, permissions, context or task direction.
entries.example: Pause analysis, inspect its status, revise the plan, change the model effort, then resume the same investigation.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Command names are not audit controls by themselves. Preserve actual semantics and maturity labels; do not imply experimental remote or cloud commands are universally available.

subfeatures.audit: Manage investigation sessions and alternate approaches
Control a work approach, objective and review pass
Control effort and inspect available working context
Adjust permitted analysis actions within policy

subfeatures.codex: Agents, subagents, apps, plugins and hooks
subfeatures.audit: Manage assistance and extension mechanisms
Select identity and working scope
Personalise controls without changing audit methods
Recover or move supported sessions

audit_enhancements.change: Expose audit-friendly labels and descriptions for task controls while retaining power-user commands.
audit_enhancements.why: Users should understand execution, review and context operations without knowing developer terminology.

entries.audit_feature: Audit agent and workstream command center
entries.codex_behavior: The command center lists chats and their status on a shared local or remote server and lets a user switch into them. It is a coordination surface separate from spawning delegated subagents.
entries.trigger: The auditor opens the task command center to inspect ongoing work.
entries.audit_action: Provide one place to see active audit investigations, identify work awaiting input, and enter the relevant conversation.
entries.auditor_control: Choose which investigation to enter and respond to its questions; visibility remains bounded by accessible work.
entries.example: Move between a loan recalculation, an access review and report preparation without losing each conversation's context.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Preserve the distinction between finding a running task and directing a delegated agent. A shared server list does not by itself provide organisation-wide audit portfolio management or new access rights.

subfeatures.audit: Accessible audit workstreams by execution server
Identify work running, finished or requiring attention
Resume the chosen investigation in context

audit_enhancements.change: Display assignment and tested period beside each workstream's status.
audit_enhancements.why: Auditors need to distinguish similarly named investigations across clients and periods.

entries.audit_feature: Assistance inside an auditor's working application
entries.codex_behavior: The IDE extension provides Codex conversation and tools within supported code editors, using the open workspace and selected context. Its integration, orchestration and review features differ from desktop and CLI clients.
entries.trigger: The auditor opens an available extension in a supported working tool and asks about selected material.
entries.audit_action: Bring conversation and contextual assistance beside the work already open in an auditor's application, using supported integration mechanisms.
entries.auditor_control: Select the material and requested action, inspect proposed changes, and choose whether to apply them.
entries.example: Select an exceptions table in a supported Excel extension and ask the agent to explain differences or prepare follow-up questions.
entries.adaptation_boundary: This directly mirrors the IDE-extension experience. It is additional to shared-file assistance; basic use of saved Office files does not depend on building an add-in. Live selection and unsaved state require explicit host support.

subfeatures.audit: Conversation beside current audit work
Current artifact context under host permissions
Ask about a selected range, paragraph or slide
Inspect and accept supported changes without leaving the working tool

audit_enhancements.change: Map host selection to stable range, paragraph or slide references where the host supports them.
audit_enhancements.why: Contextual assistance must identify the precise material being discussed.

audit_enhancements.change: Expose whether context is saved file state or live application state.
audit_enhancements.why: The agent and auditor must not unknowingly work from different versions.

entries.audit_feature: Remote audit execution workspace
entries.codex_behavior: Cloud tasks run in prepared remote workspaces with selected repositories, dependencies and tools. Work can continue while the local computer sleeps, and users can inspect results and follow up on the task.
entries.trigger: The auditor starts or delegates an eligible task to a prepared cloud environment.
entries.audit_action: Execute an audit analysis or document task remotely and return its artifacts and task history for review.
outputs: Proposed changes or a review package
entries.auditor_control: Select what is provided to the remote task, follow progress, stop work and review its returned outputs.
entries.example: Run an overnight reconciliation on an approved extract and review the exceptions the following morning.
entries.adaptation_boundary: A cloud task cannot assume access to the auditor's local Excel session, local-only folders, VPN or browser sign-in. Residency, tools and permissions depend on the selected execution route.

subfeatures.audit: Reusable audit execution environment
Scoped materials for a remote analysis
Long remote analyses independent of the workstation
Review findings and request further testing in context

audit_enhancements.change: Make the supplied dataset version and procedure version visible in remote results.
audit_enhancements.why: The reviewer must know what an unattended analysis actually examined.

entries.audit_feature: Remote steering and review of audit work
entries.codex_behavior: Supported mobile and remote clients can start, steer, approve and review tasks running on a connected host or in Cloud. Execution retains the chosen host's files, tools and permissions; the mobile device is a control surface.
entries.trigger: The auditor connects from a supported remote device to accessible work.
inputs: Connected execution host or cloud task
entries.audit_action: Let the auditor monitor and steer an investigation away from the workstation while preserving its execution context.
outputs: Continued work on the execution host
entries.auditor_control: Choose the host and task, inspect what an approval authorises, and interrupt or revise the work.
entries.example: During a site visit, check an ongoing reconciliation and tell the agent to investigate one flagged branch further.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Phone access does not move all data or execution onto the phone. Mobile remote workflows and the experimental CLI remote-control command have different maturity and platform conditions.

subfeatures.audit: Direct audit work from another device
Respond to scoped requests and inspect findings
Retain the authorised data and tool environment
Move an eligible investigation with explicit context transfer

audit_enhancements.change: Present concise findings with accessible supporting evidence on the remote review surface.
audit_enhancements.why: An auditor away from the desk needs enough context to steer responsibly.

entries.audit_feature: Physical controls for audit task navigation
entries.codex_behavior: Codex Micro is a limited-run input device whose keys and other controls can reflect chat status and invoke desktop actions, skills, voice and navigation. Availability depends on hardware, companion software and operating-system permissions.
entries.trigger: The auditor presses or turns an assigned physical control.
entries.audit_action: Offer optional physical shortcuts to switch investigations, dictate instructions, invoke a procedure or inspect a task needing attention.
entries.auditor_control: Choose bindings and keep the meaning of consequential commands visible before using them.
entries.example: Bind keys to three active assignments and use a voice control to add an observation during a walkthrough.
entries.adaptation_boundary: This is retained in the feature mirror as an optional peripheral. It does not require designing new hardware, and a physical approval key cannot establish professional sign-off semantics by itself.

subfeatures.audit: Physical indicators for active audit tasks
Shortcuts to configured procedures and work controls
Navigate work and dictate observations

audit_enhancements.change: Name bindings with the audit task and action they invoke.
audit_enhancements.why: A shortcut must remain understandable when several assignments are active.

entries.audit_feature: Choice of working location and isolated analysis copies
entries.codex_behavior: A task can run in its local project directory, an isolated Git worktree, or a remote workspace created from a published environment. Supported handoff changes where work runs and which working files it uses.
entries.trigger: The auditor starts a task or moves eligible work to another environment.
entries.audit_action: Offer direct work on current artifacts, an isolated working copy for parallel investigation, or prepared remote execution.
outputs: Task context tied to its environment
entries.auditor_control: Select the environment, understand its data access, and reconcile results before replacing shared working files.
entries.example: Compare two sampling approaches in isolated work areas while retaining the original population extract.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Git worktrees remain usable for suitable versioned material. Applying isolation to complex Office files requires checking copy/version/merge behavior; neither a worktree nor a working copy is an independent confidentiality boundary.

subfeatures.audit: Work on authorised current files
Isolate competing edits or investigation variants
Run with explicitly supplied remote materials
Move eligible work while making context and file changes explicit

audit_enhancements.change: Support isolated copies or versions of supported audit artifacts with explicit reconciliation of changes.
audit_enhancements.why: Office files cannot be assumed to merge like source-code text.

entries.audit_feature: Audit agent execution loop
entries.codex_behavior: The harness maintains turn state, requests model responses, routes tool calls, applies relevant permissions, streams activity and persists supported task history. The model proposes work while tools perform permitted operations.
entries.trigger: An auditor submits a task or a configured task receives an authorised continuation.
entries.audit_action: Use the same iterative loop to inspect evidence, calculate or transform data, inspect results, revise work and explain the outcome.
entries.auditor_control: Steer the objective, set accessible resources, respond to approvals and stop work.
entries.example: Investigate a reconciliation difference by reading extracts, running a calculation, inspecting unmatched items and drafting an explanation.
entries.adaptation_boundary: The audit mirror changes tools, context and procedures while preserving the execution loop. The public harness is separate from model services, hosted integrations and the complete desktop interface.

evidence.label: Open agent harness and client boundary

subfeatures.audit: Reason over evidence and execute authorised analyses
Investigate further based on actual results
Keep actions within the task's authority
Make work inspectable and continuable

audit_enhancements.change: Supply audit procedures, artifact-aware tools and evidence context to the retained execution loop.
audit_enhancements.why: The loop is general-purpose; the relevant criteria and work objects make its assistance useful to auditors.

entries.audit_feature: Concurrent retrieval of independent audit context
entries.codex_behavior: Documented CLI changes allow independent read-only lookups, including skill, memory and conversation-history reads, to run concurrently. This is a retrieval optimisation, separate from delegated subagents and concurrent writes.
entries.trigger: A task needs several independent pieces of context.
entries.audit_action: Retrieve eligible independent guidance and task history concurrently, then combine the returned context for the main investigation.
entries.auditor_control: Choose accessible sources and inspect material used; source permissions remain unchanged by concurrent retrieval.
entries.example: Load the configured reconciliation procedure and the current task's earlier decisions at the same time.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Preserve the narrow documented scope. Do not infer safe simultaneous workbook changes, unrestricted parallel connector requests, or a guarantee that every tool read can execute concurrently.

subfeatures.audit: Retrieve relevant procedures without serial delay
Load eligible prior context alongside instructions
Main investigator reconciles the returned context

audit_enhancements.change: Retain source and assignment scope on retrieved guidance and history.
audit_enhancements.why: Concurrent retrieval must not blend another client's facts or a superseded method into the task.

entries.audit_feature: Persistent audit investigations and work turns
entries.codex_behavior: Threads can be started, read, resumed, forked, listed, archived or deleted through supported interfaces. Turns accept input, stream execution and reach completed, failed or interrupted states while retaining their thread context.
entries.trigger: Start a new investigation or send another instruction to existing work.
entries.audit_action: Maintain a continuing audit conversation across questions, analysis runs, corrections and review responses.
entries.auditor_control: Resume an investigation, fork a different approach, interrupt a turn and manage chat visibility under applicable policy.
entries.example: Resume an inventory investigation when missing count sheets arrive, retaining earlier questions and results.
entries.adaptation_boundary: A chat's current files may have changed since its earlier turn. Transcript persistence, archiving and deletion are distinct from approved workpaper retention or immutable audit records.

subfeatures.audit: Maintain and revisit investigations
Explore another approach while preserving prior conversation
Manage chat lifecycle subject to record policy
Distinguish task outcomes and unfinished analysis

audit_enhancements.change: Associate relied-on outputs with the input versions used in their turn.
audit_enhancements.why: Resuming a conversation against changed evidence should not silently reuse an old conclusion.

entries.audit_feature: Visible and steerable audit execution
entries.codex_behavior: Clients stream messages, tool activity, command output, edits and approval requests. Supported surfaces let users answer questions, send follow-ups, steer or queue instructions, and interrupt the current turn.
entries.trigger: An analysis is running and the auditor observes progress or supplies new direction.
entries.audit_action: Keep analysis visible and let the auditor correct scope, explain context or stop an unsuitable line of work as it develops.
entries.auditor_control: Inspect actual tool results, respond to the agent, and stop the task without assuming already completed actions are undone.
entries.example: During procurement analysis, clarify which cancelled orders belong outside the population and ask the agent to revise the calculation.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Progress narration does not prove an action succeeded. Interruption and queued steering must preserve partial results and make unfinished work clear; behavior depends on the execution path.

subfeatures.audit: Inspect ongoing analysis and artifact changes
Supply missing context or scoped authorisation
Refine the investigation during work
Stop further work and inspect partial outputs

audit_enhancements.change: Explain changed testing scope and identify results affected by a steering correction.
audit_enhancements.why: A revised criterion may invalidate earlier calculations even though the conversation continues.

entries.audit_feature: Reviewable audit task planning
entries.codex_behavior: Supported clients can produce a plan and clarifying questions before making changes, expose a task checklist, and let the user refine the proposed approach. The plan is working guidance generated within the task.
entries.trigger: The auditor asks for an approach before analysis or artifact changes begin.
entries.audit_action: Draft the sequence of work, identify missing evidence and propose checks that the auditor can revise before execution.
entries.auditor_control: Modify scope, methods and stopping conditions, then explicitly move from planning to execution where required.
entries.example: Plan an external-audit account analysis, identifying the assertions, supplied criteria, relevant records, procedure and expected supporting work.
entries.adaptation_boundary: This mirrors planning assistance. A model-generated checklist is not automatically an authorised engagement work program; professional approval requirements come from the applicable practice and record workflow.

subfeatures.audit: Agree the analysis approach before changing work
Resolve scope and missing evidence
Track the proposed testing steps

audit_enhancements.change: Express plans using objective, population, procedure, criteria, expected output and outstanding evidence.
audit_enhancements.why: These elements let an auditor evaluate whether a proposed analysis addresses the question.

entries.audit_feature: Persistent objectives for sustained audit work
entries.codex_behavior: Goals retain an objective, completion criteria and steering context while work continues across turns. Supported controls inspect, edit, pause, resume or clear the goal. Goal state is separate from general memory and reusable instructions.
entries.trigger: The auditor sets a sustained objective with explicit completion conditions.
entries.audit_action: Continue a bounded investigation through repeated analyses until its completion conditions are met, it needs input, or the auditor stops it.
entries.auditor_control: Inspect and revise the objective, pause or resume it, and decide when the evidence supports ending the task.
entries.example: Reconcile the approved inventory extract to its control total and explain material unmatched items within an agreed time or cost allowance.
entries.adaptation_boundary: A persistent goal is not a schedule or an event subscription. Completing a task objective does not itself approve an audit conclusion or authorise scope expansion.

subfeatures.audit: Bounded investigation outcome
Continue eligible work across task turns
Retain control of sustained audit work

audit_enhancements.change: State completion conditions in terms of reconciled populations, explained exceptions or reviewed outputs.
audit_enhancements.why: A finished command or generated report is not necessarily the requested audit outcome.

entries.audit_feature: Concurrent audit work in the background
entries.codex_behavior: Supported clients keep long commands, tasks and delegated work running while users attend to other work. Status views expose active or completed tasks and work needing attention, subject to host and client behavior.
entries.trigger: An auditor starts a longer job or multiple independent workstreams.
entries.audit_action: Run eligible independent audit tasks concurrently and surface their results or requests for input without blocking unrelated work.
entries.auditor_control: Inspect and stop each task, prioritise attention, and review results before relying on them.
entries.example: Run duplicate-payment analysis while separately drafting walkthrough questions from a process narrative.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Background execution depends on host availability and the tools used. Two jobs editing the same workbook need coordination; GUI automation may occupy the foreground rather than allowing simultaneous human use.

subfeatures.audit: Allow large analyses to finish while other work continues
Separate audit procedures running in parallel
Surface results, failures and required input by workstream

audit_enhancements.change: Identify shared-file conflicts and separate analysis output destinations before concurrent edits.
audit_enhancements.why: Parallel audit tasks may otherwise overwrite the same working file.

entries.audit_feature: Understanding an existing audit work folder
entries.codex_behavior: Codex reads and searches relevant workspace files, follows applicable repository instructions and uses attached or path-selected context to explain unfamiliar material. Actual read access depends on the execution environment and permission boundary.
entries.trigger: The auditor asks a question about an existing collection of work or supplies specific files.
inputs: Authorised source documents and data files
entries.audit_action: Find relevant material, explain how files relate, identify procedures and prior work, and ground the task in the existing audit context.
entries.auditor_control: Select sources and scope, inspect cited material, and correct the agent's interpretation.
entries.example: Explain a supplier-onboarding process using its policy, workflow narrative, configuration export and prior workpapers.
entries.adaptation_boundary: File discovery does not prove population completeness or document authenticity. Complex formats require appropriate readers, and saved-file access does not imply visibility into unsaved application state.

subfeatures.audit: Locate and read relevant evidence and workpapers
Apply assignment and method instructions
Explain unfamiliar processes, calculations or data structures
Direct the agent to specific supporting material

audit_enhancements.change: Read supported audit formats and retain references to the relevant sheet, range, page or passage.
audit_enhancements.why: Source-backed explanations require more precise references than a filename alone.

audit_enhancements.change: Report inaccessible or unreadable material separately from searched material.
audit_enhancements.why: An auditor must understand the actual scope of the investigation.

entries.audit_feature: Executable audit analysis and utility work
entries.codex_behavior: Codex can run available commands, scripts and project tools, inspect their output and use results in later reasoning. Execution and file changes remain subject to the relevant environment, sandbox and approval policy.
entries.trigger: An audit task needs calculation, transformation, validation or a supported external utility.
entries.audit_action: Write or use executable analyses to reconcile data, recalculate values, test conditions and produce reviewable results.
entries.auditor_control: Inspect methods and inputs, choose permitted execution, and verify results against known checks or control totals.
entries.example: Recalculate expected payroll amounts from approved inputs and supplied rules, then compare them with the payment extract.
entries.adaptation_boundary: The code engine is general-purpose; audit formulas and rules must come from the task's actual criteria. A successful script exit does not establish correct inputs, methodology or conclusions.

subfeatures.audit: Perform reproducible audit calculations
Use approved data, document and system utilities
Verify analysis and diagnose failed procedures
Refine the test without hiding earlier assumptions

audit_enhancements.change: Retain procedure code, input identifiers, parameters and reconciliation checks with results.
audit_enhancements.why: Another auditor needs to inspect and reperform the calculation.

entries.audit_feature: Programmatic composition of audit tools
entries.codex_behavior: Where enabled, Code Mode lets model-authored JavaScript compose tool calls through an execution host. The public configuration labels the feature under development and off by default, with controls over exposed tool namespaces.
entries.trigger: An enabled task needs to combine several permitted tool operations in a programmatic step.
inputs: Tool definitions exposed to the cell
entries.audit_action: Compose permitted retrieval and analysis operations, transform their results and return the relevant material to the conversation.
entries.auditor_control: Keep effective tool permissions visible, inspect results, and interrupt work through supported controls.
entries.example: Retrieve independent approved extracts, align their identifiers and pass only the exceptions into the next analysis step.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Keep its experimental maturity explicit in the mirror. Programmatic composition does not enlarge tool authority or guarantee cancellation of every nested operation; interruption behavior needs verification on the chosen host.

subfeatures.audit: Compose a bounded audit-tool procedure
Pass authorised results between tools
Restrict which audit tools may be composed
Stop supported execution while reporting partial work

audit_enhancements.change: Preserve provenance through intermediate transformations and composed tool calls.
audit_enhancements.why: A compact programmatic result must remain traceable to the evidence and procedure that produced it.

entries.audit_feature: Create and revise the auditor's actual work files
entries.codex_behavior: Codex creates and changes workspace files and supports inspection of changes through relevant clients. Desktop file surfaces can preview supported outputs; Git-specific actions and terminal review differ from artifact-focused editing experiences.
entries.trigger: The auditor requests a new deliverable or a revision to existing work.
inputs: Existing saved files or output requirements
entries.audit_action: Create or revise supported workbooks, documents, presentations, scripts and other files while retaining their use in existing applications.
entries.auditor_control: Review changes in the workbench or another editor, accept or revise them, and continue assistance after saving external edits.
entries.example: Update a reconciliation workbook and its report narrative, then let the auditor refine both in Excel and Word.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Baseline shared-file work requires no API to the editor. Semantic comparisons, formula preservation, macros, comments and concurrent edits require format-specific verification; Git text diffs do not establish Office-file merge safety.

subfeatures.audit: Generate workpapers, analyses and reports
Revise the auditor's current working artifacts
Review and control changes with format-appropriate support
Keep Excel, Word and PowerPoint in the working flow

audit_enhancements.change: Use format-aware comparisons for supported workbooks, documents and presentations.
audit_enhancements.why: A reviewer needs to see meaningful changes such as formulas, values and narrative revisions.

audit_enhancements.change: Detect external saved edits before applying another change.
audit_enhancements.why: The auditor and agent share artifacts and may modify them through different tools.

entries.audit_feature: Visual material as audit task context
entries.codex_behavior: Supported clients accept image inputs such as screenshots and diagrams. Attachment handling and supported formats vary by client, host and version, including differences in remote and mobile flows.
entries.trigger: The auditor supplies a screenshot, diagram or other supported image.
entries.audit_action: Interpret visible material, relate it to the task and identify what further evidence is needed to test the relevant assertion.
entries.auditor_control: Confirm the image's source and context, inspect the interpretation and supply clearer or authoritative material where needed.
entries.example: Provide a screenshot of an access-administration screen and ask which visible entitlements differ from the supplied approved-role matrix.
entries.adaptation_boundary: A screenshot may omit fields, history or population scope. Visual interpretation does not establish authenticity, completeness or that the visible configuration was active at the relevant time.

subfeatures.audit: Inspect captured application context
Understand a supplied process or system diagram
Provide visual context through supported local or remote surfaces

audit_enhancements.change: Keep image provenance, capture context and interpretation uncertainty beside the analysis.
audit_enhancements.why: Visible content alone does not establish the relevant period or completeness of evidence.

entries.audit_feature: Create explanatory audit visuals
entries.codex_behavior: Supported Codex surfaces can generate or edit images using available image tooling, including a reusable skill. Generated visual files can accompany other work; availability and usage conditions depend on the client and workspace.
entries.trigger: The auditor requests an illustration or a revision to an explanatory visual.
inputs: Source diagram or image where applicable
entries.audit_action: Produce visuals for explanations, presentations and training, keeping them distinct from captured source evidence.
entries.auditor_control: Check wording and depicted relationships, request revisions and decide where the visual will be used.
entries.example: Create a clearly labelled illustration explaining role separation in a procurement process for an advisory presentation.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Retain image generation as a general capability without treating a generated illustration as proof of how a process operates. Exact data charts and validated process models need appropriate source-backed methods.

subfeatures.audit: Create an explanatory audit illustration
Revise an authorised presentation visual
Reuse visual production instructions for audit deliverables

audit_enhancements.change: Label explanatory generated visuals distinctly from captured source material.
audit_enhancements.why: Illustrations used in reports must not be mistaken for observed evidence.

entries.audit_feature: Suggested continuations while writing audit instructions
entries.codex_behavior: Eligible desktop users can receive a suggested continuation while drafting a prompt. Accepting it places text in the composer rather than sending it. The documented beta has account, plan, age and region conditions.
entries.trigger: The auditor types an instruction in an enabled composer.
entries.audit_action: Suggest a continuation that helps the auditor articulate a task, while leaving the complete instruction editable before submission.
entries.auditor_control: Ignore or accept the suggestion, edit it and explicitly send the instruction.
entries.example: While writing a reconciliation request, accept a suggestion to include the relevant reporting period, then correct the date before sending.
entries.adaptation_boundary: A suggested prompt is neither a discovered fact nor permission to execute. Preserve the distinction between accepting draft text and submitting a task; the reference feature remains eligibility-limited beta.

subfeatures.audit: Help formulate an audit request
Retain editable user control before submission
Expose availability rather than assuming universal support

audit_enhancements.change: Keep suggested audit wording editable and distinguish it from submitted instructions.
audit_enhancements.why: Convenient drafting must not silently introduce a criterion or authorisation.

entries.feature: Web search, built-in browser, browser extension, and Computer Use
entries.audit_feature: Research and interact with relevant audit sources and applications
entries.codex_behavior: Codex distinguishes web search, a separate-profile built-in browser, approved extension access to existing browser context, and permitted desktop GUI control. These routes have different session and permission boundaries; Windows GUI control uses the foreground.
entries.trigger: An audit task requires current public information, a web workflow or authorised application interaction.
entries.audit_action: Research criteria, inspect relevant interfaces or carry out scoped application steps through the appropriate available route.
entries.auditor_control: Choose the target and action scope, approve access where needed, inspect consequences and stop the operation.
entries.example: Inspect an authorised vendor-onboarding workflow in a test environment and compare visible approval steps with its documented procedure.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Browser state, GUI state and shell networking are distinct. Treat source content as untrusted; confirm consequential actions and recorded results. Windows foreground use and macOS locked-use conditions are not interchangeable.

subfeatures.audit: Find relevant current criteria and public sources
Inspect public pages and local audit tools
Work with permitted existing tabs and authenticated sources
Observe or operate supported applications when needed
Keep research access separate from authority to change business state

audit_enhancements.change: Capture the source location, observation time and permitted action scope for a workflow observation.
audit_enhancements.why: Reviewers need to know where an observation came from and whether business state was changed.

entries.feature: Browser annotations and site integration API
entries.audit_feature: Point at a specific source passage or application object
entries.codex_behavior: Users can select page content, annotate it and send it with available context to Codex. A site integration API can customise selectable targets and metadata. This is separate from general browser actions and WebMCP tools.
entries.trigger: The auditor selects content in a supported browser surface and adds an instruction.
entries.audit_action: Anchor an audit question or revision request to the material the auditor is viewing, rather than requiring a separate description of its location.
outputs: Follow-up analysis tied to the selected material
entries.auditor_control: Choose the selection, inspect supplied context and state the requested action.
entries.example: Select a clause in an online incident-management procedure and ask how it relates to the proposed walkthrough.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Selection metadata is context, not automatic evidence capture or source authenticity. Website-defined metadata must remain distinguishable from the auditor's instructions; browser annotation does not imply connector write access.

subfeatures.audit: Ask about a particular passage or displayed object
Let supported audit pages identify meaningful selectable records
Provide relevant source context while showing what is supplied

audit_enhancements.change: Carry useful audit references such as policy section or record identifier with selected content when available.
audit_enhancements.why: A later reviewer needs to locate the material behind the question.

entries.audit_feature: Bring the current audit screen into the conversation
entries.codex_behavior: Appshots attach the frontmost window image and available accessibility text to a desktop chat. Text coverage depends on the source application; macOS/Windows permissions and client support govern availability.
entries.trigger: The auditor chooses to share the current application window with a task.
entries.audit_action: Examine the supplied screen in the context of the audit task, explain unfamiliar fields, identify apparent inconsistencies, and request underlying data when the capture cannot support a conclusion.
entries.auditor_control: Choose the window and purpose; inspect what was captured before relying on it or sharing further.
entries.example: While reviewing a loan-system rate configuration screen, ask which fields should be reconciled to the approved change request.
entries.adaptation_boundary: A capture is a limited point-in-time input. It does not establish complete configuration history, actual application execution, or access to hidden records.

subfeatures.audit: Bring the current evidence or system screen into the task
Provide readable labels and values alongside the image

subfeatures.codex: Attach the capture to a chat
subfeatures.audit: Keep the supplied screen linked to the resulting analysis

audit_enhancements.change: Attach capture time, application/source identity and declared coverage to the shared screen.
audit_enhancements.why: A reviewer needs to distinguish what was actually supplied from unseen source-system data.

entries.audit_feature: Review audit work and business changes for supported findings
entries.codex_behavior: Codex analyses repository state and tool results; dedicated review examines selected changes and returns prioritised findings without modifying the working tree. GitHub review is a separate configured entry point.
entries.trigger: An auditor requests review of a workpaper/change, or a configured review event starts it.
inputs: Selected workpaper or change and baseline
entries.audit_action: Inspect audit scripts or authorised application code directly, and adapt the same review loop to changed workpapers or business-process evidence. Test supplied expectations and return located findings, impact and proposed corrections separately from applying them.
entries.auditor_control: Select scope and criteria, challenge findings, and separately authorise corrections and professional sign-off.
entries.example: Review a revised reconciliation workbook and flag an excluded account, a broken formula, and an unsupported conclusion with cell/source references.
entries.adaptation_boundary: The review pattern transfers directly; audit-specific assertions and tests require explicit procedures and evidence. A clean review is not assurance beyond the work performed.

subfeatures.audit: Review changed cells, passages, rules, or records against their prior state
Rank evidenced exceptions under the chosen audit criteria
Return review notes before any corrective changes

audit_enhancements.change: Replace code-location review anchors with cell, document, record and evidence anchors.
audit_enhancements.why: Audit findings must be traceable to the affected work and its support.

audit_enhancements.change: Use the engagement's criteria and significance scheme for findings.
audit_enhancements.why: Developer severity labels do not determine audit significance or professional conclusions.

entries.audit_feature: Control, application-security and findings workbench
entries.codex_behavior: Codex Security provides specialised scans, change review, finding triage, remediation and verification through distinct local, cloud and programmatic surfaces. Cloud availability includes research-preview limits; it differs from Codex's own execution safeguards.
entries.trigger: The auditor starts a targeted/bulk assessment or enables an authorised change-monitoring run.
inputs: Authorised application source and revision when performing actual software-security work
entries.audit_action: Retain actual security scanning for authorised IT/IS audit of application code. Adapt the scan-and-review loop to supplied business-control procedures: consolidate exceptions, investigate evidence, propose improvements and retest while preserving coverage.
entries.auditor_control: Set scope, validate findings, accept or dispute classifications, and decide whether remediation is sufficient.
entries.example: Scan user-access extracts across several systems, investigate conflicting privileged roles, and retest an updated access population after remediation.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Actual code-security capabilities remain useful for authorised IT/IS audit. General business-control tests require different tools and procedures; their proposed mirror preserves the work loop. Enterprise risk ownership needs separate domain design, with no delivery phase selected here.

subfeatures.audit: Focused control testing and bounded population-wide checks
Investigate and classify exceptions
Propose corrective action and test supplied remediation
Produce portable findings and follow-up evidence
Retain authorised application-security assessment for IT/IS audit
Reassess the affected scope after a relevant code or business change
Compare preventive control or process improvements grounded in findings

audit_enhancements.change: Supply audit-specific control tests and population reconciliation checks.
audit_enhancements.why: A vulnerability scanner's rules cannot test arbitrary business controls.

audit_enhancements.change: Separate suggested exceptions, validated findings and retest outcomes.
audit_enhancements.why: The auditor must know which conclusions have supporting investigation and review.

entries.audit_feature: Contextual workpaper editing and review conversations
entries.codex_behavior: Desktop editing and PR Chat place supported files or pull-request context beside conversation. Users can annotate content, request changes, inspect proposed patches, and accept or reject edits in supported flows.
entries.trigger: The auditor opens an artifact or proposed change and selects content for discussion.
entries.audit_action: Keep the discussion anchored to the selected work, explain its reasoning, prepare a targeted revision, and show the proposed result before incorporating it into the working artifact.
entries.auditor_control: Edit directly or in the preferred external tool; decide which revisions to accept and separately perform any professional approval.
entries.example: Select a finding's cause statement in a Word report, ask for stronger supporting reasoning, and review the proposed wording beside its evidence.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Audit cell/document-aware review needs format-specific presentation. Accepting an edit does not sign off the workpaper, and a shared file does not require an editor API.

subfeatures.codex: Edit supported content in the desktop
subfeatures.audit: Inspect and edit supported audit artifacts in context
Anchor a review request to a specific passage or data area
Review and apply individual proposed artifact changes

audit_enhancements.change: Show format-aware changes in cells, formulas, report passages and evidence links.
audit_enhancements.why: Raw code-style patches can hide material workbook or document changes.

audit_enhancements.change: Keep edit acceptance distinct from any configured professional sign-off.
audit_enhancements.why: Accepting wording does not establish that the underlying evidence is sufficient.

entries.audit_feature: Reviewable audit deliverables in familiar formats
entries.codex_behavior: Codex produces text and file changes, with supported desktop previews and annotations for several document formats. Terminal and IDE surfaces present outputs differently and do not all offer the same visual review experience.
entries.trigger: A task produces a workbook, report, slide deck, PDF, or other supported output.
entries.audit_action: Create or revise the deliverable, present a suitable preview, support contextual feedback, and leave the saved artifact available for continued work in Excel, Word, PowerPoint, or another appropriate application.
entries.auditor_control: Choose where to review/edit, request corrections, and decide when the output is ready for distribution.
entries.example: Produce an exception workbook and committee presentation, inspect each in the workbench, then refine the presentation in PowerPoint.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Format fidelity, formulas, comments, and save/reopen behavior must be verified. Previewing an artifact does not prove all its calculations or metadata are correct.

subfeatures.audit: Produce reusable workpapers, reports, and presentations
Inspect outputs beside the conversation
Request targeted revisions without re-describing the whole deliverable
Continue reviewing the same files in existing audit tools

audit_enhancements.change: Verify round-trip fidelity for supported workbook, document and slide features.
audit_enhancements.why: Continued work in external tools depends on preserving usable artifacts.

audit_enhancements.change: Detect intervening saved changes before revising an artifact.
audit_enhancements.why: Agent output must not silently overwrite the auditor's newer work.

entries.audit_feature: Create and publish audit dashboards and lightweight tools
entries.codex_behavior: Supported Sites flows create, refine, save, and deploy websites or applications. The documented public-beta managed publishing surface differs from CLI/IDE source editing; saved non-deployed versions can be reviewed before deployment.
entries.trigger: The auditor asks for an interactive output or chooses to publish a reviewed version.
entries.audit_action: Build an explorable exception dashboard or small audit utility, inspect its calculations and interactions, revise it through conversation, then publish only through an authorised hosting route.
entries.auditor_control: Approve the data audience and release separately from creating the draft; inspect interactions and data handling.
entries.example: Create a dashboard for exploring aged reconciliations with filters and drill-through references, then publish the reviewed version for the intended team.
entries.adaptation_boundary: This mirrors a build-and-publish capability. A generated dashboard is not automatically a durable audit record system; hosting, access, and data storage remain distinct concerns.

subfeatures.codex: Create or refine an app from instructions
subfeatures.audit: Build a small audit analysis or reporting tool
Validate the interactive output before release
Publish the approved tool to its authorised audience

audit_enhancements.change: Carry source period, calculation definitions and evidence links into audit dashboards.
audit_enhancements.why: Interactive summaries need an inspectable basis for reliance.

audit_enhancements.change: Apply explicit audience and data-release choices to publishing.
audit_enhancements.why: A useful working dashboard may contain information that cannot be shared with its default audience.

entries.audit_feature: Core audit work tools available to the agent
entries.codex_behavior: Codex surfaces expose tools for files, execution, images, search and agent operations according to the environment. Tool availability, permission to use a tool, and a completed invocation are separate states.
entries.trigger: An audit task requires a supported file, calculation, search, or agent operation.
entries.audit_action: Select and call the relevant tool, inspect its result, and use the result in the next step. Keep concrete operations visible so the auditor can connect claims to actual file reads, calculations, or changes.
entries.auditor_control: Set operating scope, review consequential actions, and interrupt or redirect the task.
entries.example: Read an expenses CSV, run a duplicate-payment query, inspect candidate matches, and create a workbook for review.
entries.adaptation_boundary: An audit-facing label does not itself supply a new execution engine or permission. Domain-specific tools extend the same mechanism; their correctness needs separate validation.

subfeatures.audit: Inspect evidence and prepare working outputs
Execute reproducible analysis
Distinguish performed tests from intended work

audit_enhancements.change: Provide format-aware extraction and calculation tools with inspectable results.
audit_enhancements.why: Office artifacts and audit populations need more than plain-text editing.

entries.audit_feature: Discover and manage available audit data connections
entries.codex_behavior: Codex app integrations have catalog, installation and effective callable states. Enabled configuration, identity and policy affect access; connector traffic follows a distinct control path from sandboxed shell networking.
entries.trigger: The auditor selects a connected service or asks what sources/actions are available.
entries.audit_action: Show which integration can actually supply the requested material, use its permitted operations, and identify the acting account and destination before a side effect.
outputs: Retrieved material or confirmed action result
entries.auditor_control: Connect the intended account, limit scope, and authorise consequential writes.
entries.example: Retrieve an approved policy from a connected repository while leaving an unrelated client connection unavailable to the engagement.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Shared local files remain usable without an app connector. A catalog listing does not prove support for a particular audit object or operation.

subfeatures.audit: Discover permitted audit information sources
Explain whether a connection can perform the requested operation now
Make the acting account and record destination explicit

audit_enhancements.change: Display the client/entity scope and effective read/write actions of each connection.
audit_enhancements.why: The same app may contain data from unrelated engagements or clients.

entries.audit_feature: Connect reusable audit tools through a standard tool interface
entries.codex_behavior: Codex connects to local or remote MCP servers supplying tools, resources and prompts. Connections and authentication are explicit; tools may read or mutate systems. App-server uses a different protocol from MCP.
entries.trigger: The task needs a capability supplied by a configured MCP server.
entries.audit_action: Discover the supported operation, supply bounded inputs, execute it through the connection, and inspect the result before incorporating evidence or recording a claimed update.
entries.auditor_control: Choose trusted connections and permitted operations; review writes separately from reads.
entries.example: Use a read-only database tool to obtain a loan-rate change population, then use a separate analysis tool to test effective dates.
entries.adaptation_boundary: MCP supplies an interface, not audit semantics or a universal connector. A remote tool's authority and data path need individual assessment.

subfeatures.audit: Attach local analytics or approved remote audit services
Retrieve task references and reusable tool-specific guidance
Confirm identity and available read/write actions

audit_enhancements.change: Require source identity, extraction scope and observation time in evidence-returning tools.
audit_enhancements.why: Structured tool output needs enough context to assess relevance and freshness.

entries.audit_feature: Installable audit capability packages
entries.codex_behavior: Plugins bundle skills and other capabilities such as MCP tools, hooks or UI. Curated and team/project distribution paths exist; installing a package and authorising its capabilities are distinct, with client-specific support.
entries.trigger: The auditor or administrator adds or updates an approved capability package.
inputs: Tool credentials and policy where needed
entries.audit_action: Make packaged procedures, references and tools available to the workbench while exposing their ownership and effective permissions. Allow the team to reuse a consistent capability set across relevant workspaces.
entries.auditor_control: Choose package scope, inspect included behavior, and enable only permitted connections or actions.
entries.example: Install a team package containing access-review procedures, an approved export parser, and reporting templates.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Installation does not approve an audit methodology or grant source access. Preserve separate owners and update paths for workspace, personal and plugin-provided skills.

subfeatures.audit: Package reusable audit procedures with the tools they use
Share approved practice or team capability packages
Inspect versions, updates, disablement and removal

audit_enhancements.change: Declare supported practices, input formats, dependencies and procedure versions in an audit package.
audit_enhancements.why: A team needs to understand where a reusable package applies and what an update changes.

entries.audit_feature: Reusable audit procedures invoked through conversation
entries.codex_behavior: Skills package instructions with optional references, scripts and resources. Codex can select a relevant skill or run one explicitly requested by the user; skill ownership and distribution differ by source.
entries.trigger: The auditor invokes a procedure, or the agent recognises a matching task.
entries.audit_action: Follow the reusable procedure with the current inputs, execute permitted supporting tools, and return the procedure's expected work product and verification evidence.
entries.auditor_control: Choose or adjust the procedure and inspect its assumptions, inputs and resulting work.
entries.example: Invoke a bank-reconciliation skill with this month's statements and ledger export, then review the reconciling items in the generated workbook.
entries.adaptation_boundary: A skill guides execution and does not grant data access. Procedure criteria, version references and required task-level checks belong to the direct audit counterpart. Formal methodology governance requires separate domain design; no delivery phase is selected here.

subfeatures.audit: Run a named audit procedure
Suggest an applicable working method
Keep instructions, calculations and templates together

audit_enhancements.change: Include criteria references, required inputs, expected outputs and verification steps in audit procedure skills.
audit_enhancements.why: A reusable routine must explain what was tested and how its result should be checked.

entries.audit_feature: Teach the assistant a demonstrated audit routine
entries.codex_behavior: On supported macOS setups, Record & Replay observes a permitted demonstration and drafts a reusable skill. Later runs use current task tools and variable inputs; Computer Use availability is required.
entries.trigger: The auditor chooses to record a familiar repeatable procedure, then later invokes the resulting skill.
entries.audit_action: Capture the demonstrated steps, draft an inspectable procedure with inputs and verification guidance, let the auditor refine it, and repeat it with new values under the current task's permissions.
entries.auditor_control: Start/stop recording, inspect the generated procedure, provide new inputs, and review replay outcomes.
entries.example: Demonstrate downloading a monthly control report, filtering the period, and saving it under the engagement's naming convention.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Recording is not proof that the demonstrated method is appropriate or that replay succeeded. The reference is macOS-specific; matching it elsewhere requires investigation.

subfeatures.audit: Demonstrate an existing audit routine
Turn the demonstration into an inspectable reusable procedure
Repeat for another period, entity, or population

audit_enhancements.change: Add review of captured assumptions and validation on a second representative case before routine reuse.
audit_enhancements.why: A demonstrated path may omit exceptions or depend on unnoticed application state.

entries.audit_feature: Workspace guidance and operating preferences
entries.codex_behavior: Codex discovers applicable AGENTS.md guidance and combines configuration with managed requirements under defined precedence. Settings control models, tools, permissions and other behavior, and some configuration can live outside the project.
entries.trigger: An audit workspace or scoped task starts, resumes, or changes its applicable configuration.
entries.audit_action: Apply the relevant vocabulary, file conventions, preferred procedures and operating limits to work in that scope. Make inherited guidance inspectable when it affects an outcome.
entries.auditor_control: Maintain workspace instructions and inspect which higher-level requirements apply.
entries.example: A client workspace specifies financial year, entity naming, working-paper conventions, approved criteria references and read-only access to source extracts.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Instructions shape agent behavior; they are not by themselves enforced access controls or proof of methodology compliance. Engagement facts still need identified sources.

subfeatures.audit: Apply the relevant client, engagement and folder guidance
Combine practitioner preferences with organisational limits
Tailor operating behavior without changing the underlying workspace experience

audit_enhancements.change: Expose the effective client/engagement guidance and its provenance.
audit_enhancements.why: Auditors must identify which conventions and criteria shaped the task.

entries.audit_feature: Checks at agent workflow events
entries.codex_behavior: Hooks react to supported agent lifecycle events using configured handlers. MCP hooks use existing connections; an explicit blocking result can stop an operation, while missing tools or errors do not inherently block it.
entries.trigger: A configured agent event occurs, such as a tool call, compaction, task start or completion.
entries.audit_action: Run an appropriate contextual or output check at that lifecycle point and report its result. For example, validate a generated workpaper's required references after an edit and surface any gap before the auditor relies on it.
entries.auditor_control: Approve trusted handlers, inspect their scope, and decide how an unmet or failed check affects the workflow.
entries.example: After the agent writes an exception workbook, check that its population source and test parameters are recorded.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Lifecycle hooks do not themselves detect business events such as rate changes. Their reference failure behavior is not a fail-closed compliance guarantee or immutable audit trail.

subfeatures.audit: Check intended actions and generated work
Restore essential task guidance on continuation
Surface required completion checks and handoff information

audit_enhancements.change: Define the consequence of a failed or unavailable mandatory audit check separately from the reference hook default.
audit_enhancements.why: The current hook failure behavior does not establish that required checks ran or blocked subsequent reliance.

entries.audit_feature: A workbench client that can drive and observe the agent runtime
entries.codex_behavior: App-server exposes thread operations, streamed activity, tools, configuration and approval exchanges to a rich client over JSON-RPC. Its command and WebSocket transport are experimental; individual execution methods have different authority.
entries.trigger: The workbench starts a task, resumes work, displays activity, or answers an agent request.
entries.audit_action: Present the familiar conversational workspace while the runtime performs permitted work. Translate runtime events into understandable audit-task progress, artifact changes, input requests, errors and completion states.
outputs: Human response events and resumable work
entries.auditor_control: Steer, inspect, interrupt and approve applicable actions through the workspace.
entries.example: While testing expenses, show the active data extraction, completed calculation, missing evidence request and resulting workbook in one task.
entries.adaptation_boundary: This maps the runtime/client contract, not a selected architecture. Experimental status, service eligibility and each method's effective authority require verification; a single protocol does not imply one sandbox boundary.

subfeatures.audit: Start, continue and stop audit work
Explain actual progress and generated outputs
Let the auditor resolve a specific permission or clarification request

audit_enhancements.change: Translate runtime events into audit-task, evidence and artifact status without overstating completion.
audit_enhancements.why: Tool completion, successful analysis and accepted audit work are different states.

entries.audit_feature: Task-specific tools supplied by the audit workspace
entries.codex_behavior: The experimental dynamic-tools API lets a client describe tools and fulfil runtime tool requests through item/tool/call. It requires opt-in and is distinct from configuring an external MCP server.
entries.trigger: An agent requests a tool that the current workspace has exposed.
entries.audit_action: Expose bounded operations appropriate to the current audit context, fulfil a requested operation through the host, and return a structured result that the agent can inspect.
outputs: Tool result linked to its invocation
entries.auditor_control: Operate within the workspace's authorised scope and review consequential changes; an agent-proposed call does not determine its own authority.
entries.example: A workpaper view exposes a tool to fetch a selected sample's evidence references without giving the agent access to unrelated engagements.
entries.adaptation_boundary: The tool mechanism is a direct counterpart; specific native record operations depend on the later record-mode design. Experimental API and host-side enforcement remain unresolved implementation questions.

Perform a bounded operation under host authority
Make the result and any failed action explicit

audit_enhancements.why: Task-specific operations must not act on unrelated or stale audit material.

entries.feature: Codex SDK, non-interactive execution, and GitHub Action
entries.audit_feature: Run audit procedures from scripts and event-driven jobs
entries.codex_behavior: Codex offers SDKs, non-interactive exec and a GitHub Action for programmatic tasks. They provide distinct runtime interfaces and maturity levels, with structured events available for supported batch or CI workflows.
entries.trigger: A script, scheduler or configured external event starts a bounded job.
entries.audit_action: Run the declared analysis without an interactive foreground session, retain its structured outcome and artifacts, and route a completed, failed or needs-attention result to the auditor.
entries.auditor_control: Configure the mandate and limits beforehand; review exceptions and authorise any consequential follow-up.
entries.example: A detected approved interest-rate change starts a job that tests specified approval and effective-date controls against the relevant evidence.
entries.adaptation_boundary: The automation runner does not create an event feed or prove control compliance. Source access, duplicate-event handling and missed/failed runs require explicit design and validation. Ephemeral rollout behavior does not delete generated files, external records or other copies; retain relied-on work according to the chosen policy.

entries.feature: Task entry points from connected services

Review findings or requested work product

entries.audit_feature: Delegate parallel audit work to specialised assistants
entries.codex_behavior: Codex delegates tasks to separate agent threads and combines results. Custom agents can specialise instructions and supported model settings; they inherit parent permissions, provider and MCP connections rather than independently expanding access.
entries.trigger: The auditor or coordinating agent divides suitable work into independent tasks.
entries.audit_action: Assign separate agents to population analysis, criteria research, evidence inspection or workpaper review, track their work, and reconcile their findings into a coherent result with visible disagreements.
entries.auditor_control: Inspect delegated scope and progress, redirect tasks, and verify the synthesis before relying on it.
entries.example: One agent checks rate-change approvals, another recalculates affected interest, and a third reviews customer-notification evidence.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Parallel agents are not automatically independent assurance providers. Shared assumptions can produce correlated mistakes; formal human review remains a separate decision.

subfeatures.audit: Split evidence and testing work by question
Reuse distinct analysis or review roles
Trace a result back to the delegated work
Reconcile findings and surface disagreement

audit_enhancements.change: Require delegated results to identify evidence, method and unresolved disagreements.
audit_enhancements.why: The coordinating agent must reconcile substantive support rather than count agreeing agents.

entries.feature: Side chats, fork, and task references
entries.audit_feature: Explore audit questions without losing the main work
entries.codex_behavior: Side chats and forks create separate conversational paths for focused questions or alternative approaches. Supported clients can reference other tasks and navigate between related work without rewriting the original transcript.
entries.trigger: The auditor opens a side investigation or tries a different approach from existing context.
entries.audit_action: Investigate a specific issue separately, preserve the main engagement conversation, and bring relevant conclusions back with a clear reference to the supporting branch.
outputs: Referenced conclusion for the main task
entries.auditor_control: Choose what context is carried, compare paths, and identify which conclusion is adopted or superseded.
entries.example: Fork a sampling discussion to explore a different stratification while keeping the original test approach available for comparison.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Forking a conversation does not itself isolate working files, change permissions, or create an approved alternative procedure. Avoid treating an abandoned branch as the current conclusion.

subfeatures.audit: Investigate a narrow evidence or methodology question
Explore an alternative interpretation from the same starting context
Link the supporting investigation into the main work

audit_enhancements.change: Show which exploratory conclusion was adopted or superseded.
audit_enhancements.why: Alternative analyses must not be mistaken for the current relied-on conclusion.

entries.audit_feature: Separate working copies for parallel audit analysis
entries.codex_behavior: Git worktrees give independent tasks separate working directories in the same repository. App-managed copies can have different lifecycles; isolation and handoff behavior vary across local, remote and scheduled workflows.
entries.trigger: The auditor or agent starts parallel work that could modify overlapping artifacts.
entries.audit_action: Give each analysis a separate working copy, preserve the starting version, and compare completed outputs before integrating selected changes into the main body of work.
entries.auditor_control: Choose which changes to retain and resolve conflicting edits before replacing the shared artifact.
entries.example: Analyse alternate loan populations in separate copies of a workbook, then incorporate the selected result without overwriting the other analyst's work.
entries.adaptation_boundary: This is the isolation pattern, not a requirement to use Git for every Office artifact. Binary document merging needs format-aware handling; filesystem separation does not establish engagement confidentiality.

subfeatures.audit: Protect concurrent analysis from accidental file overwrites
Know which source version each analysis used
Reconcile completed work into the main artifact

audit_enhancements.change: Provide format-aware comparison and explicit reconciliation of Office artifact changes.
audit_enhancements.why: Separate working copies alone do not safely merge binary or structured document edits.

entries.audit_feature: Maintain task focus through long audit work
entries.codex_behavior: Codex carries instructions, conversation and tool results in active context. Automatic or requested compaction condenses earlier material for continuation; it reduces context pressure without guaranteeing that every prior detail survives.
entries.trigger: A long-running audit conversation approaches its context limit or requests compaction.
inputs: References to durable files and decisions
entries.audit_action: Continue the task from a concise state of its objective, completed work and next steps, reopening identified artifacts whenever exact evidence, calculations or wording are required.
outputs: Resumed work linked to durable artifacts
Questions where needed context is missing
entries.auditor_control: Inspect the current scope, restate a correction, and require source verification for material conclusions.
entries.example: Resume a multi-day payroll analysis with the population file, completed tests and unresolved exceptions still identified.
entries.adaptation_boundary: A condensed conversation is working context, not the evidence archive. Exact facts, approved criteria and relied-on outputs should remain in accessible artifacts or records.

subfeatures.audit: Keep the current objective and relevant work available
Continue lengthy investigations within context limits
Verify exact evidence instead of relying on a summary

audit_enhancements.change: Keep evidence identifiers, criteria references and material decisions in durable task artifacts.
audit_enhancements.why: Compaction can omit details that should remain recoverable for audit work.

entries.audit_feature: Return to prior audit work and its reasoning
entries.codex_behavior: Supported Codex clients provide thread listing, resumption, search, branching, archiving and deletion. Available operations and storage differ between local, cloud and remote environments; structured runtime history supports continuation.

entries.auditor_control: Choose what to resume, retain, archive or delete within applicable policy.
entries.example: Find the prior discussion explaining an exception rule, reopen the supporting workbook, and revise the analysis for a new period.

entries.audit_feature: Attribute unattended assurance runs to an authorised owner

entries.audit_feature: Inspect, accept and retain changes to audit work
entries.codex_behavior: Supported Codex clients expose file and branch diffs, annotations, selective staging/reversion, commits, pushes and pull requests. Review can examine selected changes without editing the working tree.
entries.trigger: An agent or auditor changes a work product, or requests review of an alternative revision.
entries.audit_action: Show what changed in workpapers, calculations, narratives and supporting scripts; let the auditor inspect changes, comment, retain selected revisions, or restore an earlier version.
entries.auditor_control: The auditor accepts or rejects changes and decides when to share the revised output. These choices remain separate from professional sign-off.
entries.example: After revising a sampling workbook, inspect changed parameters and formulas, retain the corrected calculation, and reject an unrelated narrative edit.
entries.adaptation_boundary: Preserve the review/acceptance experience. Semantic comparisons and safe merging for Office files require investigation; they cannot be assumed from text Git diffs, and auditors need not see Git terminology.

entries.feature: Workspace roles, access, and user lifecycle
